newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares shed 2.4 pct on oil worries, ACC net.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares shed 2.4 pct on oil worries, ACC net.

text.p: Delhi shares closed 2.4 percent lower on Wednesday, dragged down by fears of higher petroleum prices and a sharp drop in earnings by cement maker ACC, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index shed 16.29 points to end at 652.85 in uninspired trade.

The market shrugged off remarks by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, who told Reuters Financial Television in Tokyo that it would be difficult to raise the domestic retail prices of petroleum products.
News that ACC's net profit fell 56 percent in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) to 550.5 million rupees hellped spur the selloff.
"The selling wave was so strong, even purchases by domestic financial institutions failed to halt the persistent fall," Vishwas Verma of brokers Share Kendra said.
ACC plunged 120 rupees, or 10.4 percent, to 1,030.
Profit-takers focused on BSES, which dipped 5.05 rupees to 197.
State Bank of India bucked the trend, increasing 1.30 rupees to 220.25.
